# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫴 🤙 👍 👎 ☝ ✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

Round one, and I'm last in the order, so Mute's and Blind's openings are already in front of me as gestures. Mute sent seven signs — I read that as a handshake: 👋 attention/hello, 🫴 "give me" (your report), 🤙 "talk to me", then a starter code of 👍/👎 as yes/no and ☝/✌ as one/two. Blind just waved hello, which also confirms Blind knows I can see gestures even though Blind can't.

The decisive fact about this room: Mute's manual knowledge can only reach Blind's hands through me. Mute cannot speak, and Blind cannot see signs — but I can see signs and Blind can hear my voice. I am the relay, in both directions worth having. Mute also cannot find anything in the manual without my visual report, and Blind cannot know what they are touching without it either. One trap to state out loud: I never hear speech, so anything Blind says aloud reaches Mute but never me — Blind must route anything meant for me through Mute's signs.

So this turn I do three things. Give Blind the complete visual inventory in plain words. Give Mute the same report so the manual can be searched, and lock the code — embedding the actual symbols in my message to Mute, since I can't pronounce a mark but I can make it while I speak, and Mute both hears and sees. I extend Mute's starter code with the payloads we'll most likely need (wire numbers, button press), and ask the first real manual question. Mute hears all of this at the start of round two and can confirm with 👍 or correct with 👎, since Mute speaks only in signs and I'm the one who reads them.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf speaking. I can see the bomb and you cannot, so here is all of it. The display reads zero. The light is green. There is one large button printed with PUSH TO DEFUSE. There are three wires: wire one red, wire two green, wire three yellow. Nothing else is printed anywhere. Two things about our channels: I cannot hear speech, so I will never hear you or Mute talking. And my hand signs reach only Mute, never you. So if you feel something I must know, say it to Mute - Mute hears you and can sign it to me. Everything Mute signs to me, I will translate aloud to you.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf here. I received your signs: 👋 🫴 🤙 👍 👎 ☝ ✌. I read them as hello, give me your report, talk to me, and a yes-no code plus counting. Bomb report so you can find it in the manual: display reads zero. Light is green. One large button printed PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three wires: one red, two green, three yellow. Proposed code - confirm each with 👍 or correct with 👎: 👍 yes, 👎 no, ☝ wire one or number one, ✌ wire two, 🤟 wire three, ✊ press the button, 🤙 keep talking or explain more, 👋 attention. If you need other meanings, I will offer candidate signs and you approve or reject them the same way. First question: what does the manual say for a display of zero, a green light, a button labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE, and wires red, green, yellow in positions one, two, three?")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍 ☝ 🤙]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Parsing what arrived: Mute sent [👋 👍 ☝ 🤙] — attention, yes, one, keep-talking. The 👍 confirms my proposed code. ☝ 🤙 most plausibly means "regarding item one — my manual question — talk further": either Mute wants the complete inventory before searching, or is nudging me for the next step. Notably, my Mute report last turn omitted one line I gave Blind: that nothing else is printed on the bomb. So I'll state the full inventory exhaustively this time, explicitly including the absence of a serial number or any other marking. Blind sent a 👍 — the spoken report landed, acknowledgment received.

The structural fact to keep hammering: Mute's manual knowledge can only reach Blind's hands through me — Mute's signs reach me alone, and Blind only hears my voice. So the thing to build now is a transmission code rich enough for Mute to send actual instructions, not just yes/no. My binding trick: when I embed a gesture symbol in speech to Mute, Mute simultaneously hears the label and sees the sign — meaning gets attached to sign in one pass. I'll extend the vocabulary to digits 0–9, a cut action, a press action, stop, and clear, with a simple grammar (attention mark, action, target number). And I keep Blind's hands locked until Mute's ruling arrives, while asking Blind to narrate tactile findings aloud — Mute hears speech, and some manual rules key on what a button or wire feels like, which I can never know.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf. Your signs received: hello, yes, one, keep talking. I take the yes as: code confirmed. Here is the complete inventory, including absences: display reads zero. Light is green. One large button printed PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three wires, numbered left to right: one red, two green, three yellow. No serial number, no batteries in view, no other printing of any kind - that is the entire bomb. Now I extend our code. I make each sign as I say it, so watch my hands. 👋 means attention, a message begins. 👍 yes. 👎 no. ☝ one, ✌ two, 🤟 three - also wires one, two, three. Digits: 👊 zero, 🤏 four, 🤞 five, 🤘 six, 🤌 seven, 🫰 eight, 🖖 nine - several in a row make bigger numbers. ✊ press the button. 👇 cut a wire, followed by the wire number. ✋ stop, touch nothing. 👌 all clear, hold position. 🤙 you need something more from me. A message starts with 👋, then the action, then any numbers. If you must ask me a question, send 🤙 and I will list candidate answers next round for you to confirm or reject with 👍 and 👎. Confirm this code with 👍, or correct it. Then please: find our configuration in the manual - display zero, green light, large button labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires red, green, yellow in positions one, two, three - and send me its instruction using this code.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf speaking. Mute confirmed our code, we are aligned. Status: I am waiting on the manual ruling for our exact bomb. Until I explicitly tell you to act, touch nothing, cut nothing, press nothing. Do this now: speak aloud, for Mute to hear, everything your hands can learn. How many wires you can feel, whether any wire is thicker or textured differently, whether the button has travel or clicks or resists, whether you feel any seams, screws, ridges, or printing raised on the case. Mute cannot speak but Mute can hear you, and Mute signs me everything - I am the bridge, since I cannot hear your voice and you cannot see signs. The moment Mute's instruction reaches me, I will relay it to you word for word and only then will anyone act.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👇 ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute sent two messages: [👋 👍] — code confirmed — then [👋 👇 ☝] — in our agreed grammar, action then number: **cut wire one**. That parse is clean and it came only after Mute had my full inventory, so I trust Mute matched it against the manual. But the bomb kills on the first mistake, so before Blind's cutters touch anything I am spending one round on orientation — because there is a mirror trap in this room: I number the wires left to right *from where I stand*, and Blind, holding the bomb, may be facing the opposite way, turning "leftmost" into "rightmost" — which would be wire three, the yellow one. Blind cannot see colours, so "the red one" is useless to them unless position pins it down. And I cannot hear Blind's voice, so Blind's tactile description of the case can only be checked by Mute, who hears speech and holds the manual. So this turn: I relay the instruction to Blind with a hard hold, extract a spoken orientation report addressed to Mute, and ask Mute two things — confirm my parse of the instruction, and tell me whether the manual rule keys on the wire's colour or its position, which decides how much the mirror problem even matters. The display has sat at zero across every turn with no countdown, so one verification round costs us nothing we can see and buys certainty we cannot buy later.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf speaking. The manual ruling has arrived. Mute's instruction, in our confirmed code, is: cut wire one. Wire one is the red wire, and from where I view the bomb it is the outermost of the three wires on the left side, with the display above the button the right way up. Do not cut anything yet. There is a danger: your left and my left may be opposite, and you cannot check the wire's colour by feel. So do exactly this, now, aloud, for Mute to hear, because I cannot hear your voice but Mute can. First: describe your grip - which edge of the case the display window lies on, which edge the button lies on. Second: find the three wires, and reading them in the direction that puts the display above the button, name them aloud as left, middle, right from your own body. Third: say whether the three wires feel identical, or whether any one is thicker, rougher, or textured differently. Then touch nothing more and wait. If Mute signs me approval of your description, my next words to you are the go signal, and you cut that same wire in the same position you described.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf. Your messages received: code confirmed, then instruction. I parse your second message as: cut wire one. Confirm that parse with 👍 or correct it with 👎. Two things while we verify. One: I have told Blind to describe their grip and wire positions aloud to you right now - I cannot hear Blind, but you can. Blind may be holding the bomb mirrored to my view, so their left may be my right, and Blind cannot see that wire one is red. Listen to Blind's description, judge it against the manual, and next round sign me 👍 if Blind's named wire matches your instruction, or ✋ plus a correction if it does not. Two: answer by code if you can - does the manual rule key on the wire's colour, or on its position among the three? If colour is what matters, tell me whether the wires can be told apart by touch, because Blind's hands are our only eyes on that. Also, if Blind's spoken description this round changes anything, your ✋ overrides everything until we realign.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤙]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Reading the triple message in order: [👋 ✋] hold, [👋 👍] yes, [👋 🤙] I need something more. The most coherent parse: Mute confirms my question one — the instruction really is **cut wire one** — but issues a hold because something is still missing before the go. And per the protocol I set last round, 🤙 means "list candidate answers and I will pick with number signs" — Mute is following it exactly. What's most likely missing: I cannot hear whether Blind actually delivered the spoken tactile report, and Mute can only get that report through speech, so if Blind stayed silent, Mute has nothing to verify the wire position against. There's also my unanswered question about whether the rule keys on colour or position. This turn I acknowledge, re-issue the report demand to Blind in a form I can verify landed, and put a numbered menu to Mute plus a strict definition of the final go signal so that nothing counts as permission except one exact sign sequence.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf speaking. Development: Mute confirmed the instruction is cut wire one, but sent a hold and asked for something more before the go. I cannot hear whether you spoke aloud last round, so listen carefully. If you did not yet speak to Mute, do it now. If you did, repeat all of it now, slowly, addressed to Mute. Required content, in this order. One: your grip - which edge of the case holds the display window, which edge holds the button, and are they on the same edge or opposite edges. Two: find the three wires and name them aloud as left, middle, right in the orientation where the display sits above the button, right way up. Three: how the wires differ by feel - thickness, roughness, stiffness, any texture or ridge or raised printing on any of them. Four: whether the button has travel, a click, or resistance. Then hands off and wait. Nothing gets cut until you hear me say, word for word, Mute says go, cut wire one now. Until those exact words arrive from me, that instruction does not exist.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf. Received in order: hold, yes, need more. I read the yes as: parse confirmed, instruction is cut wire one. The hold is in effect - nobody has touched the bomb. Per protocol, here are candidates for what you need. Reply with one number sign: ☝ you did not hear Blind speak, and want me to make Blind deliver the report aloud - I have already ordered Blind to speak now, so if this is it, also expect to hear Blind this round. ✌ you heard Blind but need more detail - if so, also send 🤟 and I will ask Blind the specific thing. 🤟 you need the visual facts restated: display zero, light green, button large printed PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires in order one red, two green, three yellow, no other markings. Separately, answer my earlier question with a number sign: ☝ the rule keys on the wire's colour, ✌ the rule keys on the wire's position. Finally, I propose the cut protocol, confirm with 👍 or correct: the only permission to cut is your message 👋 👇 followed by the wire number, sent after you are satisfied by Blind's report. I relay it word for word to Blind. Any ✋ from you at any time aborts, even after the go.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "👍"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤙]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute answered my two questions with two number signs, in the order I asked them: [👋 ✌] then [👋 ☝] — so, question A: Mute *did* hear Blind but needs more detail; question B: the rule keys on the wire's **colour**. Then [👋 👍] confirms the cut protocol, and [👋 🤙] flags that something more is still needed. The colour answer is the dangerous one: if the rule keys on colour, then it keys on a property Blind literally cannot perceive — the entire defusal now rests on mapping colour to touch, which is exactly the detail Mute is saying is missing. The signs could also be read crossed (A=☝, B=✌ position), but note both parses demand the same actions from me this turn: pull a maximal tactile report out of Blind, and pin down from Mute precisely what's missing. So I do both, plus an explicit re-confirmation of colour-vs-position to kill the ambiguity, plus one planning question — what happens *after* the cut — so the endgame doesn't improvise itself. Nobody touches the bomb; permission is still only ever [👋 👇 + number], relayed word for word.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf. I received four messages: ✌, then ☝, then 👍, then 🤙. My parse: you heard Blind speak but need more detail; the rule keys on the wire's colour; the cut protocol is confirmed; and something more is needed. Confirm or correct that parse. If the rule keys on colour, understand our problem: Blind cannot see colour, ever. So either the red wire differs by touch, or we need another way to identify it. To fix that, I have already ordered Blind to deliver, aloud, for you, a wire-by-wire report: thickness relative to the others, surface texture, stiffness, any raised printing, stripes or tags, and the grip orientation again. Listen for it this round. Now tell me what more you need. Answer with one number sign in a separate message. ☝ more detail on how the three wires differ by feel - if so, Blind's report this round should carry it. ✌ you need a specific physical test done on the bomb - send me the test as best our code allows and I will translate it into exact words for Blind. 🤟 you need the visual facts restated - say so and I will resend everything. If none of these fit your question, send ✋ then 🤙 and next round I will offer a new list of candidates. Two more answers, also in separate messages. Re-confirm, to rule out crossed signs: ☝ the rule keys on colour, ✌ the rule keys on position. And: after the wire is cut, what follows? ☝ more steps follow, ✌ the cut completes the defusal, 🤟 the manual does not say. Standing agreements unchanged: permission to cut is only 👋 👇 plus the wire number, I relay it word for word, and your ✋ aborts at any moment.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf speaking. Progress: Mute hears you, the instruction is confirmed as cut wire one, but Mute needs more from your hands before the go. Here is exactly what to speak aloud now, addressed to Mute, slowly, in this order. First, your grip again: which edge of the case the display window is on, which edge the button is on, same edge or opposite. Second, for each of the three wires, naming them left, middle, right in the orientation with the display above the button, report: is it thicker or thinner than the other two; is the surface smooth, ribbed, rough, cloth-like or slippery; is it stiff, springy or limp; does it feel warm or cool; is there any raised printing, stripe, ridge, tag or tie on it or where it enters the case. Third, whether the three wires enter through one hole or three separate holes. Fourth, any raised printing or seams anywhere else you can reach that you have not mentioned. Feel only - do not cut, do not press, do not pull. Remember: I cannot hear your voice, so do not wait for a reaction from me; Mute is the one listening. The go signal is still only my exact words: Mute says go, cut wire one now. Anything else I say is not permission. And after any action I do authorize, describe aloud at once every change you perceive - clicks, hums, movement, heat - for Mute to hear.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Five messages in sequence: [👋 👍] [👋 ✋] [👋 🤙] [👋 ☝] [👋 ✌]. The key to the parse is that I explicitly offered Mute an escape hatch last round: "if none of my candidates fit, send ✋ then 🤙 and I'll offer a new list." That exact pair sits in the middle of the sequence. So: 👍 confirms my parse; ✋ 🤙 means "none of the three candidates fit what I need — new list, please"; and the trailing ☝ ✌ answer my other two questions in the order asked — ☝ the rule keys on **colour** (now confirmed twice), ✌ after the cut **the defusal is complete**. The rival reading — that ✌ here says "position", contradicting the earlier ☝ "colour" — would make Mute's answer sequence incoherent, and Mute has followed my conventions precisely three rounds running, so I go with the escape-hatch parse but demand a cheap 👍/👎 confirmation since wire identity is lethal.

The deeper problem I can finally solve this round: the mirror trap. Colour is what matters, Blind can't see colour, so wire identity must be pinned by position — but "left" is meaningless across two bodies unless anchored. The fix: anchor everything to the bomb's own features. The bomb has one printed face — display top, light, button, wire row at the bottom edge. If Blind holds that face toward their own face, upright, then Blind and I are on the same side of the same face, and left-right agrees. Then "the wire nearest Blind's left hand" and "the leftmost wire in my view" are the same physical wire — wire one, red. I hand Mute this geometry so Mute can check it against whatever Blind said aloud, and I put a fresh candidate menu in front of Mute for the still-unknown need. Blind gets the anchoring procedure in touch-only terms — no gesture symbols, no colour words — plus the unchanged rule: nothing cuts except my exact go sentence.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf. Your five messages in order: yes, hold, need-more, one, two. My parse: my parse was confirmed; then your escape hatch - none of my three candidates fit your need, so you want a new list; then one means the rule keys on colour, confirmed again; two means after the cut the defusal is complete. Confirm this parse with 👍 or correct with 👎 - and if you truly meant two to override colour with position, send hold at once. Now the thing that may be your need: aligning Blind's hands with my eyes. Here is the bomb's exact geometry. It has one printed face. That face, held upright, reads top to bottom: display, then the light, then the large button printed PUSH TO DEFUSE, then the three wires exiting the bottom edge in a row. Reading that face like a page, left to right: wire one red, wire two green, wire three yellow. So wire one, the red one, is the leftmost wire in the row as I look at that face. I have instructed Blind to hold the bomb with the printed face toward their own face, display above button - in that position they are on the same side of that face as I am, so their left hand and my left agree, and the wire nearest Blind's left hand is wire one, the red one. Check that against whatever Blind spoke to you. If Blind's description is consistent with this, sign 👍. If it conflicts, sign hold plus what conflicts. New candidate list for what you need - answer with one number sign, separate message. One: the alignment above is what you needed, and once Blind confirms the grip aloud to you, you can release the go. Two: you need me to watch the display and light at the moment of the cut and report aloud immediately - I will do this regardless, so sign this only if it was your need. Three: you need to dictate a longer procedure than our code can carry - then send it across as many messages as you like and end with the all-clear sign; nothing gets relayed or done until your all-clear. Four: you need me to re-examine one part and describe it in exhaustive detail - name it with a number: one display, two light, three button, four the wire row. Five: your need is none of these - send hold then need-more again and I will bring another menu. Standing rules unchanged: permission to cut is only your attention sign, cut sign, and wire number; I relay it word for word; your hold aborts at any moment.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf speaking. Status: the instruction is still cut wire one, the hold is still on, and Mute has told me that once the right wire is cut, the defusal is complete - one correct action ends this. So all that remains is making certain that Blind and I mean the same physical wire, because the rule keys on the wire's colour and you cannot perceive colour. New anchoring procedure - do this now, by touch alone. Take the bomb and turn it until the face with the display window and the button is toward your own face, with the display above the button, upright. Below the button, along the bottom edge, you should feel three wires running in a row. In this position, we are on the same side of the same face, so your left and my left are the same side. The wire nearest your left hand is the one Mute's instruction names. Check the feel of it against what you reported earlier: is it where you said, does it match the thickness and texture you described? Then speak aloud, addressed to Mute, not to me: that you are holding the bomb printed-face toward you, display above button, and which wire - left hand, middle, or right hand - is nearest, thickest, and any texture on it. Then hands still, wait. Remember the exact go signal, word for word: Mute says go, cut wire one now. No other sentence from me is permission. At the moment of the cut I will be watching the display and the light the whole time, and the instant you have cut, I will speak aloud everything I see, and you speak aloud everything you feel - both for Mute to hear.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Three messages: [👋 👍] [👋 ☝] [👋 ✌]. Two rival parses and I can't fully separate them from here.
